Hi Sara / WellBridge security team —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on from the call: 

1) SOC 2 status
- You asked whether we have a SOC 2 Type II report and when we expect final attestation.

2) Data retention and deletion SLAs (including backups)
- Clarification on default retention windows for application logs, operational logs, and backup snapshots, and the SLA for customer-requested data deletion.

3) GDPR / HIPAA / BAAs
- Whether Redwood supports BAA for PHI, and what deployment options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) enable BAAs.

4) Vendor questionnaire
- Please send your security questionnaire; we’ll assign our security contact and get it back to you.

What I’m attaching: product-security-one-pager.pdf (high-level artifacts). Monica from our Customer Reliability team is looped in and will provide the retention and deletion specifics below.

Proposed next steps:
- Monica to share retention policy summary and indicative deletion SLA (by tomorrow).
- If you can share the vendor questionnaire, we’ll start triaging items and propose a slot for a deeper security Q&A next week.

Open items for you: can you confirm whether WellBridge requires a formal BAA for the PoC, or whether that’s only necessary at production? Also note if there are any non-standard retention periods we should be aware of.

Thanks —

Aditya —

Thanks for the summary and for looping Monica/Ben in. A few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2: We need either a current SOC 2 Type II or an attestation timeline. For procurement to progress we typically require a Type II within contract execution or a signed remediation/attestation plan.

- Retention / Deletion: Our security policy requires a written retention schedule for logs and backups and a defined deletion SLA. Specifically, we need to know: 1) default retention for event/application logs, 2) retention for backups/snapshots, and 3) how long audit logs are available (for incident forensics).

- HIPAA / BAA: We do intend to classify the PoC as low-risk PHI processing. Please confirm whether Redwood will sign a BAA for this account on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. If a Hosted BAA is not available, we need an alternative (Dedicated or Private).

- Vendor questionnaire: we will share our standard Security Questionnaire (SPI-114) via SharePoint by EOD. Please have your security team complete section A and B and route back to security@wellbridgehealth.com.

Two quick asks for your team before we schedule the deeper call:
1) A short doc that maps default retention windows to system components (logs, KV cache, embeddings, backups).
2) A clear deletion SLA for customer-initiated deletes (including timelines for primary data vs backups).

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Sara
Senior IT Risk Manager
WellBridge Health
sara.ellen@wellbridgehealth.com

(Will send the vendor questionnaire link shortly.)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data lifecycle & retention questions (WellBridge)

Hi Sara — thanks for the specifics. Below is a concise mapping and our standard behaviors; we can tailor any of these in contract for Dedicated/Private deployments. Attaching a short retention_policy_summary.pdf and our SOC2 roadmap spreadsheet for visibility.

Default retention mapping (Hosted) — subject to contractual adjustment:
- Application / request logs (access logs, API request metadata): default 30 days online, aggregated logs retained for 12 months in archived storage.
- Audit logs (security/audit trails): retained 12 months; available for export upon request (export typically provided as CSV/JSON).
- Inference artifacts (temporary inputs/KV cache): ephemeral by design — KV cache evicted within 24 hours for regular requests; embeddings persisted only if explicitly stored by the customer (not by default).
- Backup snapshots (system backups of model artifacts/config): default retention 90 days; immutable snapshots retained per backup cycle.

Deletion & SLA:
- Customer-initiated deletion requests for primary customer-controlled data: standard SLA is 5 business days to remove data from active serving and indexes, plus up to 30 days for all backups and archival copies to be purged.
- If expedited deletion is contractually required (e.g., HIPAA workflows), we can add a 72-hour SLA for primary data in Dedicated/Private and negotiate reduced backup purge windows.

SOC 2 status:
- Redwood has engaged an external auditor; Type II assessment in progress with expected report date Q4 2027.
- We can provide interim artifacts: control mapping, SOC 2 readiness checklist, and recent internal audit summaries (see soc2-roadmap.xlsx).

HIPAA / BAA:
- Redwood will sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted accounts, BAAs are available on enterprise plans with account-level contractual controls; we can route through legal. Please flag if WellBridge requires Hosted BAA for the PoC — we can prioritize.

Encryption / KMS:
- By default we manage keys. Customer-managed keys (KMIP / cloud KMS integrations) are available for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps we propose:
- You to share the SPI-114 questionnaire (we’ll complete A/B sections within 3 business days).
- Security deep-dive call — suggested slot: Friday 2027-07-23 10:00 AM PT (30–45m).
- Aditya to coordinate legal for BAA language if needed.

Internal note: Ben — pls confirm if we should include expedited deletion terms in the PoC SOW or reserve for production contract language.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood-inference.com
